claims.evidence: The witness identified a 4-cylinder engine but could not confirm the brand or specific vehicle fitment.
No engine code stamping or model identification was read by the witness.
The presence of spark plug wires instead of individual ignition coils suggests an older generation engine design.
The origin of the engine (local vs. imported) cannot be determined through photos alone.
A guarantee is a verbal contract and cannot be verified by visual inspection of the item.

risks.risk: Internal engine sludge or poor maintenance.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the underside of the oil filler cap and the visible internals through the oil hole.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a professional internal cleaning or potential rebuild.

risks.risk: Low compression or blown head gasket.
risks.proof: A video clip of a compression test being performed on all cylinders.
risks.if_unproven: as a non-running core for parts only.

risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine model code stamped onto the engine block.
A video showing the crankshaft being rotated manually with a breaker bar.

proof_requests: Photo of the engine model code stamped on the block (e.g., where it says '5S').
Photo of the oil filler hole with the cap removed to check for sludge.
Video of the engine being turned over manually to ensure it is not seized.
Close-up photos of the intake and exhaust ports to check for carbon buildup or oil residue.
response.reason: The witness could not identify the brand or model of the engine. Without confirmation of the specific engine code, it is impossible to determine if this is the high-demand Toyota 5S-FE or a less valuable unit.
